activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 7 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: A neutral tone necessarily proves that a report contains no bias.
cards.explanation: Tone is one clue; selection and omission can still introduce bias.

cards.statement: A message can have a large reach and still be misleading.
cards.explanation: Large distribution does not guarantee accuracy.

cards.statement: Reach measures the number of people who receive a message.
cards.explanation: Reach is a measure of audience size.

cards.statement: A headline is normally a long list of sources at the end of an article.
cards.explanation: A headline is the title above a news story.

cards.statement: Misinformation is always created with a proven intention to deceive.
cards.explanation: Deliberate deception is associated with disinformation; misinformation may be shared unknowingly.

cards.statement: A persuasive advert aims only to provide neutral data.
cards.explanation: Persuasive communication aims to influence its audience.

cards.statement: A claim never needs evidence.
cards.explanation: Claims often need evidence to be assessed.

activities.explanation: Cada carta repasa una regla del tema; revisa las falladas al terminar el mazo.

activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 8 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: Fact-checking is the same as sharing a claim immediately.
cards.explanation: Fact-checking requires checking before accepting or sharing information.

cards.statement: Disinformation involves deliberately misleading information.
cards.explanation: Intentional deception distinguishes disinformation.

cards.statement: A headline can attract attention without presenting the full context.
cards.explanation: Headlines are brief and may omit important background.

cards.statement: The audience can influence vocabulary, examples and tone.
cards.explanation: Communicators adapt messages to their intended audience.

cards.statement: A report can support a claim while still admitting that more evidence is needed.
cards.explanation: Careful reporting distinguishes support from complete proof.

cards.statement: Fact-checking involves checking information against evidence.
cards.explanation: Fact-checking tests whether a claim is accurate.

cards.statement: Evidence is an uncountable noun in phrases such as a piece of evidence.
cards.explanation: The natural count expression is a piece of evidence.

cards.statement: Bias always means that every fact in a report is invented.
cards.explanation: Bias can affect selection or wording without making every fact false.

activities.explanation: Cada carta repasa una regla del tema; revisa las falladas al terminar el mazo.

activities.instructions: Desliza a la derecha si la frase es correcta y a la izquierda si no lo es.
activities.prompt: Mazo de 5 afirmaciones para repasar el tema.

cards.statement: A source is where information comes from.
cards.explanation: A source provides or originates information.

cards.statement: A source can be checked for reliability before it is used.
cards.explanation: Checking origin and independence helps assess reliability.

cards.statement: Tone describes the emotional or attitudinal quality of a message.
cards.explanation: Tone can be neutral, critical, sarcastic or alarmist.

cards.statement: Context can help readers understand what a statistic means.
cards.explanation: Background information supports accurate interpretation.

cards.statement: Evidence can include reliable figures or documents.
cards.explanation: Evidence is material used to support or test an idea.
